content.value_statement: LLM evaluation quality often drops when judges use vague rubrics or biased comparisons. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through scoring, pairwise review, bias mitigation, and metric selection.
actual_capabilities: Selects direct scoring or pairwise comparison for different evaluation tasks.
Defines weighted criteria and calibrated rating scales for LLM judges.
Designs pairwise comparison flows with position swapping and consistency checks.
Creates domain-specific rubrics with score levels, examples, and edge cases.
Maps evaluation tasks to precision, recall, F1, agreement, and rank metrics.
Explains mitigation steps for position, length, verbosity, and self-enhancement bias.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete hosted evaluation service.
Example scripts are demonstrations and need adaptation before production use.
Evaluation reliability still depends on representative data and human validation.
Bias mitigation reduces known problems but cannot remove all judge errors.

use_cases.title: Compare Model Responses
use_cases.description: Use pairwise review to choose the better answer for tone, clarity, usefulness, or preference quality.

use_cases.title: Build Evaluation Rubrics
use_cases.description: Create clear scoring levels, observable criteria, and edge case guidance for repeatable reviews.

use_cases.title: Audit Judge Reliability
use_cases.description: Check automated judge results against human labels and find systematic bias patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Evaluation Method
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new evaluation task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an evaluation method for [task]. The outputs are [objective or subjective]. Explain the best metric and why.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Scoring Rubric
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a repeatable direct scoring rubric.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a balanced rubric for [criterion] in [domain]. Use a [scale] scale and include edge case guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Model Outputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Response A and Response B for [criteria]. Include position bias mitigation and explain the final confidence.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Evaluation Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an evaluation pipeline for [product workflow]. Include validation, judge selection, bias controls, metrics, and human review triggers.

output_examples.input: A team needs to grade customer support replies for accuracy and helpfulness.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends direct scoring with separate weighted criteria for factual accuracy, completeness, tone, and actionability.

output_examples.input: Two chatbot answers differ mainly in style and clarity.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends pairwise comparison with swapped positions, tie handling, and confidence based on consistency.

output_examples.input: A judge agrees with humans overall but fails on concise answers.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies length bias risk and recommends explicit conciseness criteria plus disagreement analysis by response length.

best_practices: Require evidence-based justification before every automated score.
Swap response order in pairwise comparisons and map results back before deciding.
Validate automated judge outputs against human labels before using them for decisions.
anti_patterns: Using one vague quality score for many unrelated criteria.
Trusting a single pairwise pass without checking position bias.
Treating high agreement as sufficient without inspecting systematic failure cases.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps design LLM-as-judge evaluations for scoring, comparison, rubrics, metrics, and bias mitigation.

faq.question: Does it run evaluations automatically?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples. Users must connect the approach to their chosen model APIs and data.

faq.question: When should I use direct scoring?
faq.answer: Use direct scoring when criteria are objective, such as format compliance, accuracy, safety, or instruction following.

faq.question: When should I use pairwise comparison?
faq.answer: Use pairwise comparison for preference judgments, such as tone, clarity, persuasiveness, or style.

faq.question: How does it reduce evaluator bias?
faq.answer: It recommends position swapping, explicit length guidance, blind review, cross-model judging, and confidence calibration.

faq.question: Can it replace human evaluation?
faq.answer: No. It should be calibrated against human judgments and routed to human review for low-confidence cases.
